cream-paper.$description: Cream Paper — Page canvas and primary surface — warm off-white that softens the otherwise stark black/orange system

card-white.$description: Card White — Elevated card surfaces and input backgrounds — sits one step above the cream canvas

pebble-gray.$description: Pebble Gray — Secondary surface for section bands, subtle backgrounds behind grouped content

linen-border.$description: Linen Border — Hairline dividers, card borders, and table separators — the dominant structural line color

ash.$description: Ash — Disabled controls, placeholder shapes, and de-emphasized borders

ink.$description: Ink — Primary headings, body text, and the near-black terminal panel background

graphite.$description: Graphite — Dark elevated surfaces for code blocks and terminal mockups

carbon.$description: Carbon — Secondary text, button text on light backgrounds, icon strokes

slate.$description: Slate — Muted helper text and meta-information

stone.$description: Stone — Tertiary captions, timestamps, inactive nav items

fog.$description: Fog — Light placeholder text, icon tints on muted backgrounds

signal-orange.$description: Signal Orange — Orange supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

ember.$description: Ember — Hover state for Signal Orange, secondary highlight orange for icons and micro-emphasis

apricot.$description: Apricot — Lighter orange for inline links, secondary text accents, and warm icon strokes

burnt-orange.$description: Burnt Orange — Deep orange for borders on featured elements, hover borders, and dark-mode accent strokes

persimmon.$description: Persimmon — Darkest orange for high-contrast text accents on light surfaces and breadcrumb separators

peach-blush.$description: Peach Blush — Pale orange wash for decorative borders and soft highlight backgrounds

teal-token.$description: Teal Token — IDE syntax-highlight color for strings and identifiers in code blocks — repeated at scale gives the page its terminal texture

sky-token.$description: Sky Token — IDE syntax-highlight for keys, booleans, and object properties in code blocks

orchid-token.$description: Orchid Token — IDE syntax-highlight for keywords and function names in code blocks

forest.$description: Forest — Green supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Use as a supporting accent, not as a status color

success-green.$description: Success Green — Green supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Use as a supporting accent, not as a status color

coral-alert.$description: Coral Alert — Red supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Use as a supporting accent, not as a status color

rose-blush.$description: Rose Blush — Red supporting accent for decorative details and low-frequency emphasis. Use as a supporting accent, not as a status color

inter.$description: Primary UI and editorial typeface — handles all headings, body text, buttons, and navigation. Weight 600 is the default for headlines, weight 400 for body, weight 500 for labels. Calt and liga features are disabled, giving the type a more uniform, 'engineered' feel rather than the swashy alternates Inter ships with.

jetbrains-mono.$description: Developer-language typeface — owns the eyebrow labels ('I'M A DEVELOPER'), code blocks, terminal output, API URLs, and visitor IDs. Acts as a visual signature: whenever the page shifts from prose to technical content, JetBrains Mono takes over. Weight 470 is the distinctive 'regular' weight that sits between 400 and 500.
